---
title: "Improving stopped-path bookkeeping"
subtitle: "Original versus survivor-index implementation"
---

## What changes?

The original stopped estimator reconstructs the active indices from all ruin times
at every step. It then checks again that active paths have not previously ruined.
The new `estimate_ruin_survivors()` starts with all indices active and removes
newly ruined paths after each step. Active paths are therefore known survivors.

Increment generation, likelihood weights, and contribution summaries are unchanged.
Survivors keep their original order, so identical seeds should give exactly the
same random paths and results. This experiment investigates runtime only; the
statistical estimator and its variance are unchanged.

```{r}
#| label: comparison-setup
for (file in c("model.R", "importance_sampling.R", "stopped_survivors.R")) {
  source(file.path("project_B", file))
}
library(ggplot2)
if (!requireNamespace("ggbeeswarm", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Install ggbeeswarm before rendering this report.")
}
theta_grid <- c(-0.55, -0.30, -0.10, 0)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 12, fig.height = 5)
```

## Check that results are identical

Before timing, compare individual contributions, ruin times, simulated step counts,
and summaries at each tilt. Each pair uses seed 5301 plus its grid index and 2,000
paths. `identical()` checks the complete returned object, not merely agreement
within Monte Carlo uncertainty. The separate test suite also covers all-ruin and
no-ruin cases (`Rscript tests/run_tests.R` from the assignment root).

```{r}
#| label: comparison-correctness
checks <- data.frame(theta = theta_grid, identical_results = FALSE)
for (i in seq_along(theta_grid)) {
  set.seed(5301 + i)
  original <- estimate_ruin(2000, theta_grid[i], "stopped", diagnostics = TRUE)
  set.seed(5301 + i)
  improved <- estimate_ruin_survivors(2000, theta_grid[i], diagnostics = TRUE)
  checks$identical_results[i] <- identical(original, improved)
}
stopifnot(all(checks$identical_results))
knitr::kable(checks, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Paired timing experiment

We use 150,000 paths per batch and 15 repetitions at each of four tilts:
120 timed batches in total. Seed 5201 determines randomized pair and execution
order. Each original/improved pair uses the same seed and random draws. Warm-up,
garbage collection, seed initialization, and equality checks are outside timing.
Every pair also verifies exact summary equality. All reusable code lives in
`B/stopped_survivors.R`.

```{r}
#| label: comparison-benchmark
raw <- benchmark_stopped_versions(theta_grid, n = 150000, repetitions = 15, seed = 5201)
summary <- summarize_stopped_benchmark(raw)
knitr::kable(summary, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
if (min(raw$elapsed) < 0.05) {
  cat("Some batches are shorter than 0.05 seconds; increase n for stronger timing evidence.")
}
write.csv(raw, file.path("report", "stopped_benchmark_raw.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(summary, file.path("report", "stopped_benchmark_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Beeswarm comparison

Every dot is one timed batch. Boxplots summarize the repetition distribution;
all panels share the same vertical scale. The plot displays marginal timings,
while speedups in the table use matched original/improved pairs.

```{r}
#| label: comparison-beeswarm
#| fig-cap: "Original and survivor-index runtimes across four tilts; lower is faster. Identical seeds give identical simulation workloads within each pair."
raw$implementation <- factor(raw$implementation, levels = c("Original", "Survivor indices"))
raw$tilt <- factor(sprintf("theta = %.2f", raw$theta),
                   levels = sprintf("theta = %.2f", sort(unique(raw$theta))))
p <- ggplot(raw, aes(implementation, elapsed, color = implementation)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.45, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.12) +
  ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm(size = 2, cex = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~tilt, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Original" = "#D55E00", "Survivor indices" = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(title = "Does maintaining survivor indices reduce runtime?",
       subtitle = "Stopped estimators: 150,000 paths per batch; 15 paired repetitions per tilt",
       x = NULL, y = "Elapsed seconds per batch",
       caption = "") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none",
                                      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
p
ggsave(file.path("report", "figures", "stopped_survivors_beeswarm.png"), p,
       width = 12, height = 5, dpi = 180)
```

## Interpretation

The median paired time saving ranges from
**`r round(min(summary$median_paired_time_saved_pct), 1)`%** to
**`r round(max(summary$median_paired_time_saved_pct), 1)`%** across these settings.
Positive savings and speedups above one favor survivor indices; negative savings
mean the new implementation was slower. Exact results match, so measured differences
come from implementation cost and timing noise rather than different simulated paths.

Maintaining survivors avoids repeated full-vector scans and a redundant crossing
check. Filtering the remaining indices still costs time, so gains depend on tilt
and sample size. These local measurements do not guarantee the same speedup on
another machine. Raw and summary CSV files are saved beside this report, and
`figures/stopped_survivors_beeswarm.png` is saved for slides.
